newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest products notionally steady late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest products notionally steady late.

text.p: U.S. Northwest products were notionally steady on Thursday, with diesel prices poised to fall after rallying earlier in the week.
"(Seattle is) the highest priced diesel market in the West Coast," one trader said.

A rash of refinery problems this summer and news that the Olympic Pipeline in Western Washington state would close part of its line next week for repairs, forced diesel traders to buy up the product. Low sulphur diesel in Seattle was assessed between 83 and 85 cents a gallon. Regular unleaded gasoline was pegged 72.50 to 73.50 cent a gallon, up from late last week.
